name: token-count
axis: tokenising character state machine over a large ASCII text
notes: globals.vl is the SAME program written at top level (every binding a wasm module global instead of a function local), present only to price the known global/local cliff; it measured 0.95x here. A 1_000_000-char ASCII text with irregular spacing, tokenised PASSES times (n = characters scanned). The state machine is hand-written in all four so the algorithm is identical; Rust's split_whitespace() and Python's str.split() are library routines with a different cost model and were measured separately rather than substituted. Python runs PASSES=50, a 20x reduction. VL has no split builtin at all - std:fmt's split() allocates a slice per scan position, so a hand state machine is the only sane VL spelling.
